A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCP/LUR forecasting-evaluation framework and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material and v3's appended studies can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic experiments, forecasting evaluations on eight real-world datasets, and sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds entropy-metric comparisons, long-history experiments, TimerXL evaluation, and a nonlinear synthetic study.

M1.justification: Equation 8 changes SCP from 1 minus normalized reference error to its maximum with zero, altering the defined output when the original expression is negative. Algorithm 1 still omits clipping, so implementation propagation is unclear. The spectral calculations, LUR, and Appendix B extensions remain unchanged; C.7 tests the existing nonlinear extension.

E1.justification: The eight real-world datasets are retained. Appendix C.7 adds a synthetic scenario with nonlinear polynomial dependence, extending the earlier linear Gaussian and sinusoid-mixture studies. Longer histories are settings changes. The TimerXL experiment does not identify its dataset, so it does not establish additional real-world dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.4/Table 7 introduces direct comparisons against permutation entropy, weighted permutation entropy, and sample entropy using DLinear errors on ECL. v2 discussed entropy approaches without this empirical comparison, so this adds a substantive comparator family. The original five-forecaster comparisons remain unchanged; Appendix A.2's seven-to-five edit corrects their stated count.

E3.justification: Added experiments use ETTm1 histories of 336–2048 with horizon 336, TimerXL with history 96 and horizons 96–720, and three controlled nonlinear feature representations. Table 8 adds wall-clock timing. Existing benchmark splits and protocols remain unchanged. Equation 8 revises SCP's evaluation definition, but the PDFs do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: C.5 extends the existing history-length sensitivity analysis to longer contexts and measured computational scaling. C.7 adds a previously absent ablation comparing original, insufficient nonlinear, and sufficient nonlinear feature spaces. Together these substantially expand empirical validation of scalability and the nonlinear extension; earlier Welch, band-partition, and multivariate-input analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-trial toy-study averaging and standard-deviation reporting, including the 640-sequence multivariate experiment. The added studies introduce no stated repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and Figures 1–7 retain their results. New Table 7 adds entropy correlations from -0.008 to 0.252 alongside retained MSElb correlations of 0.864–0.909. Tables 8–10 add runtimes of 0.121–0.556 ms, TimerXL correlations of 0.8972–0.9341, and SCP increasing from 0.1312 to 0.9911 across feature representations. These broaden the evidence rather than demonstrate same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Equation 8 substantively revises the mathematical definition by clipping SCP at zero, addressing negative values permitted by the previous expression. The Bayes-risk reasoning and Appendix B derivations remain unchanged, with no new proof. Algorithm 1 and the appendix formulas are not updated consistently.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: efficient SCP, frequency-resolved LUR, alignment with forecasting errors, predictability drift, and stratified architectural comparisons. The added experiments support these claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 qualifies the mean-shift-augmented error as a conservative surrogate relative to a chosen stationary-linear reference. Section 4.2 softens LUR near one from implying optimality to suggesting it, and recognizes cross-channel linear dependencies as another explanation for LUR above one. C.6 newly limits foundation-model conclusions and identifies transfer and pretraining overlap as unresolved issues.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code/data availability statement and repository link, specifies the Platinum 8358P CPU at 2.60 GHz for timing, and documents the nonlinear signal, feature polynomials, coefficients, and noise distribution. Existing setup details are largely retained. New-study documentation remains incomplete, including the unnamed TimerXL evaluation dataset.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al. (2022), Davenport Jr et al. (1958), and the Timer-XL paper. Section 2 reframes the contrast with prior predictability research around realized forecasting performance, regime-dependent model behavior, and drift, replacing a broader statement that existing proxies fail to supply suitable error bounds.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized related-work and method prose revisions, four appended experimental subsections, a corrected backbone count, acknowledgements, and updated correspondence/publication text. The main section sequence and most narrative wording remain intact.

P2.justification: Four compact appendix tables, Tables 7–10, are added. Existing figures and table formats are retained, while several main-text floats change column or position and surrounding text reflows. There is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the previously largely conceptual entropy comparison with direct evidence, validates the existing nonlinear extension, and adds practical scaling measurements and a code/data access statement. Its more qualified linear-reference interpretation is helpful. The gain remains limited by incomplete new-study settings, notably the missing TimerXL dataset, and inconsistent propagation of Equation 8's clipping into Algorithm 1 and the appendices. Overall, the additions modestly strengthen an otherwise largely unchanged paper.
